 Second-String Savior: Peck, Bench Deliver in Penalties, Send Toms River East to State Final 
 Matt Manley | November 19, 2026 | Last Updated November 19, 2026 
 COLUMBUS, N.J. — The last time Toms River East junior goalkeeper Mike Peck stepped into game action with the outcome in doubt, he was part of the second of two penalty-kick heartbreaks for his Raiders team within a calendar year.
 On Wednesday at Northern Burlington High School, Toms River East was one made shot by Northern Burlington away from a third straight tournament ouster on penalty kicks and its hopes rested on a player who had watched the entire 100 minutes of soccer from the bench.
 In the days and weeks prior to that moment, however, Peck had solidified his role as a penalty-stopper during practice and on Wednesday, with a trip to the NJSIAA Group III championship game on the line, Peck proved he could deliver in the most pressure-packed moment while his Raiders proved they are not cursed when it comes to penalty kicks.
 Peck saved the fifth and sixth attempts of the shootout by Northern Burlington to clinch a 4-3 win on penalties, which results in a 2-1 victory for Toms River East that sends the Raiders to their first NJSIAA group championship game since winning the overall Group IV title in 1985.
 Mike Peck saves the 5th and 6th shots of the shootout and Toms River East is headed to the Group 3 final with a 2-1 win, 4-3 on penalty kicks. https://t.co/2qAWlahwT1
 — Matt Manley (@Matt_Manley) November 18, 2026 
 “I just believed in my team,” Peck said. “I knew they were going to at least get to the pens and I know how I can do in pens. I was hoping they could pull out the win in the first eighty, but they didn’t, which is fine. That’s soccer. Twenty more minutes, couldn’t get it done, so I knew I had to come up big and I’m pretty sure I did.”
 Toms River East cashed in its first three kicks of the shootout thanks to conversions by junior Brennen Hutton, senior Ayden Salazar and senior Malcolm Smith, which gave the Raiders a 3-2 lead through three rounds. Northern Burlington goalkeeper James Murray then saved Toms River East’s fourth and fifth attempts of the shootout, which gave Greyhounds senior and second-leading scorer Monroe Castor a chance to win the match on his team’s final attempt. Instead, Peck made a diving stop to his left to extend the game into a sixth round of penalties.
 “It’s still the same mindset: you’ve got to go in there and stop shots,” Peck said. “It’s what I’ve been doing since I was four.”
 Mike Peck with a save on the 5th NB kick saves the game. Onto the sixth round of kicks. https://t.co/GSYHXXL4Hj
 — Matt Manley (@Matt_Manley) November 18, 2026 
 “Every day in practice, you can tell: he is good at pens,” Smith said. “He saves everything in practice. It’s annoying when you have to go against him.”
 Konopka sent out four new shooters onto the field for the sudden-death portion of the shootout and sophomore Jack Gillen drilled his kick to put the Raiders ahead, 4-3, in the shootout. With a chance to now win the game with a save, Peck stopped a rip by Northern Burlington senior Joe Stevens with a lunge to his left, setting off another celebration for Toms River East.
 “A lot was running through my head, especially with their student section there and everybody from my school,” Peck said. “A lot goes through your head, but you learn how to keep calm in those situations.”
 Peck and sophomore Connor Minelli began the season splitting games in goal, which ended with Minelli played both halves and overtime in Toms River East’s Shore Conference Tournament semifinal game vs. Manasquan. That game went to penalty kicks and Peck switched in to play goal during the shootout, which Manasquan won to advance to the SCT championship game. Since then, Minelli has been the primary goalkeeper while Peck has stayed ready for another chance to propel his team to victory in a round of penalty kicks.
 “The Shore Conference loss hurt,” Peck said. “I knew I had to come up big for this one and redeem myself. I think I could have done better in that game. In this one, I couldn’t have done better. I couldn’t ask for anything more.”
 “Michael and Connor, while they compete, they are very good teammates to each other,” Konopka said. “Connor was the first one out to celebrate Michael’s save and the other day, Michael was the first one out to celebrate with Connor when we won against Absegami.”
 “I know I can put my stamp on any game,” Peck said. “Connor has been the man and I’m the man for pens, and I showed it.”
 “We practice penalty kicks every other day for the last four weeks of practice. I always knew Michael was going to be the guy if it got to that point. He made huge saves. Talk about a guy rising up to the moment; it doesn’t get bigger than that.”
 Toms River East’s recent shootout misfortune prior to Wednesday was not limited to this year’s SCT. In last year’s South Jersey Group III semifinals, Delsea knocked out the Raiders on penalties after a 1-1 draw during the 100 minutes of action.
 After the loss to Manasquan in the SCT, Konopka evaluated how he laid out the plan for penalty kicks, but the practice and the process for the players was already sound.
 “I have my list of shooters and when I reflect back on what happened against Manasquan, I wasn’t prepared to go past that,” Konopka said. “So I was kind of flustered when we went past the first five. Today, I had my first five and if we needed to keep going, I would have my next five and we had an order to it. Everyone knew where they were shooting, up to ten. Hopefully, we didn’t need to go past that and fortunately, we didn’t.”
 Facing the prospect of a third straight loss via penalty kicks in a tournament semifinal, Toms River East’s shooters rose to the occasion. While Peck stepped up after spending the game on the bench, Smith was Toms River East’s bench player to deliver on the shooting side. Smith is typically Konopka’s first player off the bench and he only moved to the bench after a red card in September cost him two games.
 “Everybody has a role to play on the team,” Konopka said. “Those roles can change game-by-game, week-by-week, month-by-month. Malcolm is a kid who, we kind of got along without him when he got the red card and it just worked itself out that he finds himself more on the sideline than on the field, but he is a senior, he is a captain and he has grown so much as a person. While he is not having a whole lot of time on the field, with four minutes left in the second overtime, I said to him, ‘Are we good?’ He goes, ‘Coach, I’m locked-in.’ He knew that he was going to take a kick and he really embraced that moment.”
 “We seemed to always fall short on pens and it’s always the semifinals for some reason,” Smith said. “This year, we just wanted it more than every team. Last year, in June, I knew, which is why I started telling coach, telling all the guys: ‘We’re going to win a state championship.’ I knew what we had coming back this year. We lost big people, but who we had coming up and stepping up. This team being so close and playing together our whole lives, I knew what was going to happen. Once I said it out loud, I set the bar for everybody and everyone knew what the deal was this year.”
 While Gillen made the final kick of the shootout, his fellow sophomore delivered Toms River East’s regulation goal. Nico Pedalino collected a deflected cross from Gillen and slammed a shot from 12 yards out into the far-right corner for a 1-0 lead in the 43rd minute. The goal marked the second straight Toms River East game in which Pedalino scored the first goal of the match. Pedalino recorded a goal and an assist in Saturday’s 3-1 sectional championship win vs. Absegami.
 For the second straight game Nico Pedalino gives Toms River East a 1-0 lead, this time in the 43rd minute at Northern Burlington. https://t.co/q9apNPOOXu
 — Matt Manley (@Matt_Manley) November 18, 2026 
 “They are competitors,” Konopka said of the Gillen-Pedalino sophomore duo. “They want to win and they blend so well with the juniors and seniors that we have. It’s great to see them clicking at the same time. We’re playing some of our best soccer and those young guys are a big part of that.”
 Three minutes after Pedalino opened the scoring, Northern Burlington leveled the score on an own goal created by a dangerous corner kick by senior Lukas Kekesi that redirected into the goal off a Toms River East defender.
 Northern Burlington was once again missing leading scorer Elijah Font, who suffered a season-ending knee injury just before the start of the NJSIAA Tournament. Without its top scoring threat, the Greyhounds managed just four shots in 100 minutes, but got stellar defense and midfield play, led by senior Gino Santise.
 Junior Brady Gillen and senior Nick DiMeola were Toms River East’s defensive lifelines, with the Raiders shutting down the Greyhounds attack outside the own goal.
 Toms River East will march on to Sunday’s Group III championship game against defending group champion Ramapo, which dismantled Middletown South, 5-1, in last year’s state final to complete a 21-1 season. At 17-3-1, this year’s Ramapo team has not been as overpowering as last year’s version, but will still represent Toms River East’s toughest test of the season.
 “This is our last shot,” Peck said. “Now, we’re in the state finals. We have proved we can hang with the big teams and that we’re one of those big teams. We are the biggest team in New Jersey and I promise you, we’re going to win that final.”
